title: Composition coherence of normalized product, signed Roos cone and derived-limit comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, with exact countable products [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal S$ be an abelian category, and assume that the ordinary unbounded derived categories of $\mathcal S$, $\mathcal A$ and $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ exist [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-inverse-system, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Let $U:\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ be additive and exact. For $i=0,1,2$, let $F_i:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ be additive exact functors preserving countable products, $G_i:\mathcal S\to\mathcal S$ additive exact functors, and $b_i:F_i^{\mathrm{Tow}}U\xrightarrow{\sim}UG_i$ natural isomorphisms of strict tower functors, where $F_i^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ applies $F_i$ levelwise. Suppose $d:F_1F_0\xrightarrow{\sim}F_2$ and $t:G_1G_0\xrightarrow{\sim}G_2$ are natural isomorphisms satisfying, for every $M\in\mathcal S$,
$$b_{2,M}\circ d^{\mathrm{Tow}}_{UM}=U(t_M)\circ b_{1,G_0M}\circ F_1^{\mathrm{Tow}}(b_{0,M}).$$
Use the same letters for termwise complex functors and their exact derived functors [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Put $L=R\lim\circ U:D(\mathcal S)\to D(\mathcal A)$.

For a strict tower complex $X$ with transitions $v_n$, set $P_X=\prod_nX_n$ termwise, $s_X((x_n))=(v_nx_{n+1})$, and $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1]$ [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Fix the signed coordinates
$$H(X)^q=P_X^q\oplus P_X^{q-1},\qquad D(x,y)=(dx,(1-s_X)x-dy).$$
On strict tower maps $f$, $H(f)$ is diagonal with product map $P(f)$ on both coordinates. Use the normalized natural identification $\theta_X:R\lim X\xrightarrow{\sim}H(X)$ whose inverse carries $(\iota z,0)$ for a K-injective tower to its ordinary-limit class [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. For every complex $M$ of $\mathcal S$, define the canonical product comparison $\psi_{i,M}:F_iP_{UM}\to P_{UG_iM}$ by
$$\operatorname{pr}_n\psi_{i,M}=(b_{i,M})_n\circ F_i(\operatorname{pr}_n).$$
Then $\psi_{i,M}$ is an isomorphism, natural in strict system chain maps. It satisfies
$$\psi_{i,M}F_i(s_{UM})=s_{UG_iM}\psi_{i,M}.$$
The diagonal maps with entries $\psi_{i,M}$ in degrees $q$ and $q-1$ define natural chain isomorphisms $\kappa_{i,M}:F_iH(UM)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(UG_iM)$ with zero off-diagonal entries. The canonical exact-product total-limit comparison, with the normalization of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit], is represented by
$$a_{i,[M]}=\theta_{UG_iM}^{-1}\circ[\kappa_{i,M}]\circ F_i(\theta_{UM}):F_iL[M]\xrightarrow{\sim}LG_i[M].$$
Here $[M]$ and $[\kappa]$ denote derived localization, and the canonical exact-functor localization identifications are included. These maps descend naturally to $a_i:F_iL\xrightarrow{\sim}LG_i$ on all of $D(\mathcal S)$.

The following three compositor identities hold, with $T_M=U(t_M)$ on strict tower complexes:
$$\psi_{2,M}\circ d_{P_{UM}}=P(T_M)\circ\psi_{1,G_0M}\circ F_1(\psi_{0,M}),$$
$$\kappa_{2,M}\circ d_{H(UM)}=H(T_M)\circ\kappa_{1,G_0M}\circ F_1(\kappa_{0,M}),$$
$$a_{2,C}\circ d_{LC}=L(t_C)\circ a_{1,G_0C}\circ F_1(a_{0,C}),\qquad C\in D(\mathcal S).$$
The first two are equalities of entire strict complex maps; in the second, both diagonal entries agree and both off-diagonal entries are zero. The last is an equality of specified natural derived morphisms, with no boundedness, constructibility, or faithfulness assumption on evaluations.

proof.text: Use the exact termwise derived factorizations of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] for $U,F_i,G_i$ and $F_i^{\mathrm{Tow}}$. The latter is exact because kernels and cokernels of towers are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. In the coordinates $(y,z)$ in degree $q$ of [def-weil-strict-roos-model], set $(x,y')=(z,-y)$. Its differential $(-dy-(1-s)z,dz)$ becomes $(dx,(1-s)x-dy')$. The inclusion of the ordinary limit becomes $(\iota,0)$, and a diagonal product map remains diagonal after this change. This fixes precisely the signed coordinates and normalization used in the statement; rename $y'$ as $y$.

proof.text: Write $X=UM$, $Y=UG_iM$, and $\phi_{i,X}:F_iP_X\to P_{F_i^{\mathrm{Tow}}X}$ for the canonical product comparison. By preservation of countable products this is an isomorphism. The unique map with the prescribed projections is $\psi_{i,M}=P(b_{i,M})\phi_{i,X}$; its inverse is $\phi_{i,X}^{-1}P(b_{i,M}^{-1})$. For a chain map $f:M\to N$, the $n$th projections of $P(UG_if)\psi_{i,M}$ and $\psi_{i,N}F_iP(Uf)$ agree by naturality of $b_i$ and functoriality of $F_i$. Product uniqueness gives equality. Applying this equality degreewise to the differential, whose compatibility with $b_i$ is its naturality for $d_M^q$, shows that $\psi_i$ is a chain map. This is an elementary use of the defining product universal property, with no assertion that derived evaluations are faithful.

proof.text:
Let $v_n$ and $w_n$ be the transitions of $UM$ and $UG_iM$. Strict tower compatibility [def-weil-inverse-system] says $w_n b_{i,M,n+1}=b_{i,M,n}F_i(v_n)$. Consequently both $n$th projections of $\psi_i F_i(s_{UM})$ and $s_{UG_iM}\psi_i$ are $b_{i,M,n}F_i(v_n)F_i(\operatorname{pr}_{n+1})$. Thus the shift square commutes, as does its $1-s$ square by additivity. Using the canonical biproduct identifications for an additive functor, define $\kappa_i(x,y)=(\psi_i x,\psi_i y)$. Directly,
$$D\kappa_i(x,y)=(\psi_i dx,(1-s_Y)\psi_i x-\psi_i dy)=\kappa_i F_i(D)(x,y).$$
It is a chain isomorphism with diagonal inverse $\psi_i^{-1}$, and its naturality follows on both coordinates from step 2. These are equalities of maps to biproducts; the coordinate notation denotes the corresponding projection identities [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. In Lean, apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-roos-chain-maps] to the explicit signed coordinate isomorphisms and compose its cone comparison with H(b). Its projected coordinate identities and product uniqueness give the two full coordinate identities.

proof.text:
Fix a degree and let $\pi_n:P_{UM}\to(UM)_n$ and $\pi'_n:P_{UG_0M}\to(UG_0M)_n$ denote the projections. The $n$th projection of the left side of the product compositor identity is
$$b_{2,M,n}F_2(\pi_n)d_{P_{UM}}=b_{2,M,n}d_{(UM)_n}F_1F_0(\pi_n),$$
by naturality of $d$. The $n$th projection of its right side is
$$T_{M,n}b_{1,G_0M,n}F_1(\pi'_n)F_1(\psi_{0,M})=T_{M,n}b_{1,G_0M,n}F_1(b_{0,M,n})F_1F_0(\pi_n).$$
The hypothesis on $b,d,t$ identifies the last expressions. Product uniqueness proves the identity in every degree, hence as entire chain maps since all displayed factors are chain maps by steps 2 and 3. The hypothesis applies to $M^q$ in each degree, and naturality applies to its differential, so this also covers unbounded $M$.

proof.text:
Under the additive biproduct identifications, naturality of $d$ for both inclusions into $H(UM)^q=P_{UM}^q\oplus P_{UM}^{q-1}$ says that $d_{H(UM)}^q$ has diagonal entries $d_{P_{UM}^q}$ and $d_{P_{UM}^{q-1}}$ and zero off-diagonal entries. By [def-weil-strict-roos-model], $H(T_M)$ is diagonal with entries $P(T_M)$. Hence in degree $q$ the two diagonal entries of
$\kappa_{2,M}d_{H(UM)}$ and $H(T_M)\kappa_{1,G_0M}F_1(\kappa_{0,M})$
are exactly the two product equalities of step 4, in degrees $q$ and $q-1$. Their off-diagonal entries are zero because each factor is diagonal. The four biproduct components determine a map, proving the entire strict cone identity. Step 3 already checked its compatibility with the signed differential.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-strict-roos-derivation] for the actual strict Roos functor H, obtaining a descent CF, a factorization kappa, and the right-derived unit Q(iota) kappa. Uniqueness of total right derived functors gives rho:CF ≅ RL, with Q(iota) kappa rho = eta on every complex. Set theta=(kappa rho) inverse; then eta theta=Q(iota). The coefficient category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], hence has enough injectives. Apply the already proved private roos_inclusion_quasiIso helper of [lem-weil-strict-roos-derivation] to every K-injective tower. Its hypotheses require neither injective terms nor K-injective resolutions of the tower category; exact countable products and enough injectives of the coefficient category suffice. This proves the quasi-isomorphism clause directly. The signed inclusion formula is step 1 and its localization normalization is eta theta=Q(iota). The duplicate limit_unit_iso and roos_tower_grothendieck arguments are unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok and proof; normalized exact-product comparison as stated in lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit.

proof.text: The termwise functors in step 1 invert quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The Roos construction descends on $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$ and $\theta$ is natural there by [lem-weil-strict-roos-derivation]. Thus the conjugation of the strict cone comparison from step 3 by theta and the exact-functor factorization isomorphisms is a natural isomorphism after precomposition of $F_iL$ and $LG_i$ with the localization $Q_{\mathcal S}$: strict naturality of $\kappa_i$ is step 3. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to these two functors and this transformation, including the canonical exact-functor factorization isomorphisms. It gives a unique natural isomorphism $a_i:F_iL\to LG_i$ with those components. The same localization property applied to the termwise isomorphisms $d$ and $t$ gives their derived natural isomorphisms with exactly their degreewise representatives. It respects composition and identities, hence includes the canonical identifications for composite exact functors. In particular naturality of $a_i,d,t$ holds for arbitrary derived morphisms and inverses of localized quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Compute on $C=[M]$, suppressing localization brackets and the canonical factorization isomorphisms of step 7. Put $X=UM$, $Y=UG_0M$, $Z=UG_1G_0M$, $W=UG_2M$, and $T=U(t_M):Z\to W$. Expand the right side of the desired derived identity using step 6:
$$L(t_C)\theta_Z^{-1}\kappa_{1,G_0M}F_1(\theta_Y)F_1(\theta_Y^{-1}\kappa_{0,M}F_0(\theta_X)).$$
The adjacent factors $F_1(\theta_Y)$ and $F_1(\theta_Y^{-1})$ cancel. Naturality of the normalized comparison [lem-weil-strict-roos-derivation] gives $L(t_C)\theta_Z^{-1}=\theta_W^{-1}H(T)$. Therefore the expression becomes
$$\theta_W^{-1}H(T)\kappa_{1,G_0M}F_1(\kappa_{0,M})F_1F_0(\theta_X)
=\theta_W^{-1}\kappa_{2,M}d_{H(X)}F_1F_0(\theta_X),$$
where the equality is localization of the entire cone identity of step 5. Naturality of derived $d$ for $\theta_X:L[M]\to H(X)$ changes its last two factors to $F_2(\theta_X)d_{L[M]}$. The result is $a_{2,[M]}d_{L[M]}$. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] now proves equality of the two natural transformations on all $D(\mathcal S)$. Only strict products and biproducts were tested by projections; the passage to derived maps uses naturality and cancellation of isomorphisms.
